blocks.text: Gurbakhsh Singh and the Singhs did not blink, bow their heads, or look behind; they kept moving forward until the Pathans fled, unable to withstand the Singhs’ sword blows. From a distance the Pathans fired guns and arrows, wounding him so badly that the wounds could not be counted.

Shots cut through his flesh and bones, yet he did not accept defeat or show pain. Blood poured from his body like oil from a press and water from a pierced pouch, but Gurbakhsh Singh kept moving forward rather than turn back.

As his strength failed, he prayed that the Guru preserve his honor and accept his martyrdom. More Gilja Pathans arrived, lifted Singh bodies on spears, and Gurbakhsh Singh struck again, cutting through lances while refusing to chase fugitives or let anyone say he had retreated.
